findings.evidence:
`pkg/expression/util.go:555-563` reassigns the argument scalar function type pointer: `newArgFunc.RetType = newArgFunc.RetType.DeepCopy()` before `BuildCastFunctionWithCheck`.
`pkg/expression/scalar_function.go:350-374` shows `ScalarFunction.Clone()` keeps `RetType: sf.RetType` and clones `Function`, with an explicit invariant comment: `ScalarFunc.RetType == ScalarFunc.builtinFunc.RetType`; `GetType()` returns `sf.RetType`.
`pkg/expression/builtin.go:433-445` shows builtin signatures keep their own `tp` pointer and clone it shallowly (`b.tp = from.tp`).
`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:183-220` calls `PropagateType(ctx.GetEvalCtx(), types.ETReal, sig.getArgs()...)` for CAST-to-REAL from DECIMAL.
`pkg/expression/expression.go:1220-1263` mutates `args[0].GetType(ctx)` (i.e., the Expression’s `RetType`) but does not touch builtin signature `tp` directly.
Runtime precision/rounding depends on builtin signature `tp` in many places, e.g. `pkg/expression/builtin_arithmetic.go:809-820` uses `s.baseBuiltinFunc.tp.GetDecimal()` for decimal division rounding.
findings.fix: Avoid only reassigning `newArgFunc.RetType` (which can desynchronize `ScalarFunction.RetType` from the embedded builtin signature `tp`). Instead, deep-clone/rebuild the `ScalarFunction` so that both `sf.RetType` and `sf.Function`’s internal `tp` point to the same (new) `FieldType` object. Practical approaches: (1) introduce a helper to deep-clone a `ScalarFunction`’s ret type while updating the embedded `baseBuiltinFunc.tp`, or (2) rebuild the scalar function via the proper constructor path so the builtin signature is created with the deep-copied `FieldType` pointer.
findings.impact: Potential correctness / MySQL-compatibility regression when CAST-to-REAL relies on `PropagateType` to increase inner decimal precision: after this change, `PropagateType` can end up mutating only `ScalarFunction.RetType` while the actual runtime rounding logic still consults the builtin signature’s `tp`, making propagation ineffective and creating inconsistent planning vs execution type metadata. This risk is especially plausible in `ColumnSubstituteImpl` paths (e.g. view/derived-table column substitution) where CAST nodes are rebuilt around reused scalar-function arguments.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `master` at `cc8c83b19ce641149d370895a24578c56fd5daaf`: `pkg/expression/util.go` still contains the same `newArgFunc.RetType = newArgFunc.RetType.DeepCopy()` block with no accompanying builtin-signature `tp` synchronization.
findings.verify: Add a regression test that exercises `ColumnSubstituteImpl`-triggered CAST rebuild where the substituted argument is a DECIMAL-producing `ScalarFunction` (e.g. `a/36000`) and then CAST to DOUBLE/REAL; assert the resulting value matches the high-precision expectation (as described in `PropagateType`’s comment) and remains stable across repeated executions (to catch shared-state mutations).
findings.what: `ColumnSubstituteImpl` deep-copies and reassigns `ScalarFunction.RetType` for substituted CAST arguments, but does not keep the builtin signature return-type pointer (`builtinFunc.getRetTp()` / embedded `baseBuiltinFunc.tp`) in sync. This breaks the documented implicit invariant (`ScalarFunc.RetType == ScalarFunc.builtinFunc.RetType`) and can cause later type propagation (e.g. `PropagateType` for CAST-to-REAL) to update only `sf.RetType` while runtime evaluation/rounding still uses the builtin signature’s `tp`.

subject: expression: fix unexpected modification of shared return type of cast expr (#63072)
summary: Adds `FieldType.DeepCopy()` (parser/types) and uses it in `ColumnSubstituteImpl` when rebuilding CAST nodes to prevent shared `RetType` mutation; adds an integration test for deep-copy correctness in a view/join scenario.
